chapter: Germany, Buck's death and ideas about life
title: Accused of being drunk; the lieutenant and the glass thrown at Mrs. Valente
summary: Cast members told the lieutenant he was drunk, but another guest backed him; later a glass was thrown at Mrs. Valente at the same club, proving it was a bad place.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Now do you know what all the people in the show had in mind, I was drunk. I wasn't drunk, never was so sober in my life. But I don't know they was going to say this when they get back to the office to Mrs. Reddy, that was the lieutenant's name, Lt. Reddy. I didn't think they were going to tell her this, 'cause I wasn't drunk. But they told her I was drunk.
So the piano player, he could understand English, but he was German, he didn't say a word about nothin' he kept neutral, okay. I told her she could verify it by him. He didn't

verify it. But when this fellow called Red Knight was there and heard her tell him about what had happened with John Bubbles -- he stood her down because they were her guests, this Red Knight was her guest there and when they got through telling her about me and she went and told all the rest of them, 'Look, if I hear anything about John Bubbles again, I'm going to cancel the entire show and I'm going to get you off the bases, you're not going to play the base no more.'
So, man, they were scared to breathe where I was concerned the next time I went out on the show.

I went back to that same club again and I sat in the car while they did the show, 'cause they don't want to see me in there no more, and I don't want no more myself. But those in there don't know I'm in the car. They think the whole show is in there. They're in there to see the show they wouldn't be seeing me nohow.
So they all come out and somebody had thrown a glass and hit Mrs. Valente in the face with a glass. Then they knew that was a bad club.

When they got on the bus after the show, they got on the bus and told me about this. I asked them, was she drunk? No, she don't drink, old lady -- daughter, Katerina Valente, husband, her son -- oh, no, she don't drink.

However, George, they got the bus back to headquarters and they had to report what had happened with her about getting hit. So, therefore, something must have been wrong with that club according to me if they did that to her. So Red Knight had already told her about me, so she knew that I was right. Then they wanted me to stop with them to get themselves a drink on the way back or get a sandwich or something and I wouldn't get out and get with 'em. I got out of the bus and went over to the bus driver and I sat down at his table.
I didn't sit with the actors, I sat with the bus driver and had a sandwich and a cup of coffee, but I didn't bother the actors, no more to do with it.
